item.title: Nepse rises 48.57 points; turnover rises to Rs 8.29 billion
item.dc:creator: bishnu

item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: The Nepal Stock Exchange (Nepse) index surged 48.57 points, or 1.87%, to close at 2,633.62 points on Tuesday, as investor confidence improved following the unveiling of a plan to strengthen and revive the capital market.

This was the biggest intraday gain since August 17, when the index had closed 79.74 points higher.

The benchmark index started the day on a particularly strong note, gaining 86.05 points, or 3.32%, during the 15-minute pre-open session on Tuesday. A total of 285,810 units worth Rs 12.35 million were traded during the pre-open session.

The index, however, pared some of its pre-open gains during regular trading. It reached an intraday high of 2,679.54 points before settling at 2,633.62.

Market activity also picked up significantly, with total turnover nearly doubling to Rs 8.29 billion, the highest since April 16, compared to the previous session. A total of 20.39 million units were traded on the bourse through 78,869 transactions. Unit prices of 265 stocks advanced during the session, while 12 declined and one remained unchanged.

The market rally came a day after the government unveiled the Capital Market Strengthening and Revival Action Plan, 2026, which includes measures to improve capital market functioning and boost investor confidence.

The action plan proposes introducing a price discovery mechanism for initial public offerings (IPOs), implementing margin lending and short selling, developing the corporate bond market and opening the secondary market to non-resident Nepali (NRN) investors.

It also includes measures to expand the participation of institutional investors and modernize the Nepal Stock Exchange, CDS and Clearing Ltd (CDSC) and securities brokerage businesses.

Among individual stocks, Dibyashwori Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha Ltd posted the highest gain of 14.96%. Sindhu Bikash Bank and Multipurpose Finance Company Ltd followed with gains of 11.03% and 9.73%, respectively.

On the other hand, 8.5% Everest Bank Debenture led the losing stocks, going down by 5.55%. 10% KBL Debenture 2090 and Bottlers Nepal (Balaju) Ltd followed with losses of 3% and 2.97%, respectively.

Reliance Spinning Mills Ltd topped the turnover chart with transactions worth Rs 327.01 million. Shivam Cements Ltd and Api Power Company Ltd followed with turnovers of Rs315.70 million and Rs284.42 million, respectively.

All 13 sub-indices posted gains on Tuesday. The biggest gain came from the Non-Life Insurance sub-index, which rose 2.82%. The Life Insurance and Investment sub-indices followed with gains of 2.59% and 2.52%, respectively.

Investors said the measures announced in the government’s action plan could help make the capital market more transparent, competitive and investor-friendly while creating new avenues for investment.

Tuesday’s strong market response suggests that investors are closely watching the implementation of the government’s proposed capital-market reforms.

item.title: India okays export of up to 654 MW to Nepal
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: India has approved the export of up to 654 MW of electricity to Nepal for 18 hours a day until December 31, citing damage to Nepal’s hydropower infrastructure caused by recent floods. According to India’s Ministry of Power, the approval is effective from September 13, 2026, and allows up to 600 MW of electricity […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: India has approved the export of up to 654 MW of electricity to Nepal for 18 hours a day until December 31, citing damage to Nepal’s hydropower infrastructure caused by recent floods.

According to India’s Ministry of Power, the approval is effective from September 13, 2026, and allows up to 600 MW of electricity to be exported through the Muzaffarpur-Dhalkebar 400 kV double-circuit transmission line and up to 54 MW through the Tanakpur-Mahendranagar 132 kV single-circuit line.

The electricity will be supplied from midnight to 6 p.m. each day. The quantum of power to be exported from January 2027 onward will be reviewed in December, the ministry said.

The decision comes after recent floods caused significant damage to hydropower infrastructure on the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli River corridor in Nepal. The devastating floods of August 26 damaged 11 hydropower projects with a combined capacity of more than 400 MW. The floods caused an estimated damage of Rs 134.69 billion in the energy sector, according to the Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment report released by the government.

“The approval will help Nepal meet its power requirements during this difficult period and further strengthen the close and longstanding energy cooperation between India and Nepal,” the ministry added in the statement.

item.title: Bhotekoshi flood prompts NRB to recognize climate risk
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has expanded its risk-management rules for banks and financial institutions (BFIs) by introducing dedicated provisions for technology and climate risks. The move comes shortly after the devastating Bhotekoshi floods of August 26, which exposed the growing risks that extreme weather events can pose to financial institutions and their operations. The […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has expanded its risk-management rules for banks and financial institutions (BFIs) by introducing dedicated provisions for technology and climate risks.

The move comes shortly after the devastating Bhotekoshi floods of August 26, which exposed the growing risks that extreme weather events can pose to financial institutions and their operations.

The updated Risk Management Guidelines replace the 2018 framework and broaden the range of risks that BFIs must assess and manage. The previous guidelines recognized five traditional risk categories: credit risk, liquidity risk, operational risk, market risk, and interest rate risk.

The new framework aims to promote a stronger risk-management culture, setting minimum supervisory standards and helping financial institutions prepare for emerging threats, according to the central bank.

Under the climate-risk provisions, boards of directors must assess how climate-related risks could affect their credit, market and operational portfolios. BFIs are also required to establish a Climate Risk Committee that meets at least once every quarter to oversee climate-related risks and ensure that their exposure remains within the institution’s risk appetite.

The guidelines require BFIs to clearly assign responsibilities for managing climate risks under the three lines of defense model. They must also continue to follow the Environmental and Social Risk Management (ESRM) Guidelines, 2022 when assessing loans.

The new rules also encourage BFIs to make their physical infrastructure more resilient to climate-related events, including floods, and promote investments in energy-efficient assets to reduce long-term operational losses.

According to the NRB, financial institutions should strengthen the resilience of their assets and incorporate climate-related insights into their risk-management practices to mitigate potential losses, ensure business continuity and meet evolving regulatory and sustainability expectations.
They should also periodically conduct awareness programs on climate-exposure risks within their institutions and among relevant stakeholders.

In addition, financial institutions should foster a strong risk-awareness culture and continuously build their capabilities and expertise in managing climate-related and environmental risks in line with international standards.

NRB has also introduced stricter requirements for managing technology risks. The provisions cover risks arising from cyberattacks, system failures, data breaches and digital fraud.

Under the new framework, boards of directors are responsible for overseeing technology-risk management and ensuring that banks have adequate resources and budgets for cybersecurity. BFIs are also expected to follow recognized international security standards, including ISO/IEC 27001, as well as relevant Basel guidelines.

Banks must align their technology strategies with their broader operational-resilience plans and maintain policies covering access controls, data protection, incident response and risks associated with third-party service providers.

According to the NRB, the expanded framework is intended to ensure that BFIs are better prepared not only for traditional financial risks but also for disruptions arising from climate change and rapid technological change.

item.dc:creator: bishnu

The benchmark index remained mostly positive throughout the trading session. It opened at around 2,559 points and climbed to an intraday high of 2,587.34 points before easing slightly toward […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: The Nepal Stock Exchange (Nepse) index extended its gains for a second consecutive session on Monday, climbing 25.55 points, or 0.99%, to close at 2,585.04.

The benchmark index remained mostly positive throughout the trading session. It opened at around 2,559 points and climbed to an intraday high of 2,587.34 points before easing slightly toward the close.

The Sensitive Index, which measures the performance of blue-chip companies, also gained 0.99%.

Market breadth was strongly positive on the week’s first trading session, with 226 stocks advancing, while 47 declined and two remained unchanged. Total turnover improved to Rs 4.68 billion compared to the previous session, with 11.6 million units traded across 49,074 transactions.

Among individual stocks, Infinity Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha posted the biggest gain of 6.43% on Monday. Next were Trishuli Jalvidyut Company Ltd and Srijanshil Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha Ltd, with gains of 6.38% and 5.93%, respectively. Upakar Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha, on the other hand, posted the largest loss of 8.23%. Aviyan Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha and Sunrise Focused Equity Fund were next, with losses of 5.22% and 5.11%, respectively.

NRN Infrastructure & Development Ltd logged the session’s highest turnover at Rs 249.07 million. Liberty Energy Company and Sanima Middle Tamor Hydropower Ltd followed with turnovers of Rs 238.41 million and Rs 203.84 million, respectively.

Except for the Mutual Fund sub-index, which fell 0.31%, all sub-indices ended the session in the green. The Finance sub-index posted the biggest gain of 1.67%. Next were the Non-life Insurance and Life Insurance sub-indices, with gains of 1.51% and 1.45%, respectively.

item.title: Nepal section of New Butwal-Gorakhpur transmission line completed
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: The Millennium Challenge Account Nepal (MCA-Nepal) has completed construction of the 18 km section of the cross-border New Butwal-Gorakhpur transmission line. The completion of the Nepal section of the transmission line marks an important milestone in Nepal’s efforts to strengthen its electricity network and expand cross-border power connectivity, MCA Nepal said in a statement […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: The Millennium Challenge Account Nepal (MCA-Nepal) has completed construction of the 18 km section of the cross-border New Butwal-Gorakhpur transmission line.

The completion of the Nepal section of the transmission line marks an important milestone in Nepal’s efforts to strengthen its electricity network and expand cross-border power connectivity, MCA Nepal said in a statement on Monday.

The 18-kilometer transmission line is a part of the 138-kilometer 400-kV New Butwal-Gorakhpur transmission line. A joint venture of the Nepal Electricity Authority and the Power Grid Corporation of India is building the remaining 120-kilometer stretch of the transmission line.

“MCA-Nepal accelerated construction of the 18-kilometer section in response to a request from the Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation and has completed the work within the agreed timeframe,” it added in the statement.

Speaking at an event organized in Nawalparasi West to mark the completion, Finance Secretary and Chairperson of the MCA-Nepal Board, Ghanashyam Upadhyaya, highlighted the importance of the milestone and appreciated the partnership between Nepal, the United States and MCC. “On behalf of Nepal, I would like to express our sincere appreciation to the US Government for its longstanding commitment to Nepal’s development and its continued support through the MCC Nepal Compact,” he said. “The completion of this transmission line is an important milestone in strengthening Nepal’s electricity infrastructure and advancing cross-border energy connectivity.”

MCA-Nepal Executive Director Khadga Bahadur Bisht said the achievement reflects MCA-Nepal’s commitment to delivering on the priorities of the government.

Similarly, MCC Resident Country Director Diane Francisco thanked those who contributed to the successful completion of the Nepal section of the transmission line. “This achievement is a testament to what can be accomplished when we work together toward a shared goal,” she said.

According to MCA Nepal, the transmission line will undergo the remaining steps required before it can be energized and put into operation, including work and approvals needed to enable electricity to flow across the Nepal–India border.

item.title: Most of the trekking areas safe and operational, says TAAN
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: The Trekking Agencies’ Association of Nepal (TAAN) has said that several major trekking regions of the country, including Everest, Kanchenjunga, Makalu, Rolwaling and Helambu, continue to operate normally after the August 26 flood. Issuing a situation update on Friday, TAAN said western and far-western destinations such as Dhaulagiri, Dolpo, Rara, Jumla, Humla, Khaptad, Badimalika, […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: The Trekking Agencies’ Association of Nepal (TAAN) has said that several major trekking regions of the country, including Everest, Kanchenjunga, Makalu, Rolwaling and Helambu, continue to operate normally after the August 26 flood.

Issuing a situation update on Friday, TAAN said western and far-western destinations such as Dhaulagiri, Dolpo, Rara, Jumla, Humla, Khaptad, Badimalika, Api and Saipal have also reported no impacts or disruptions.

“We are aware of the concerns over the devastating flash floods that struck the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river corridors. Although the major Trishuli flood has already subsided, minor landslides and road disruptions exist along specific transit routes,” TAAN said in the situation update.

The autumn season of Nepal’s tourism begins in mid-September and continues through mid-December.

According to TAAN, although destinations such as Langtang and Gosaikunda are entirely safe, their standard access road through Battar, Dhunche and Syabrubesi is closed due to flood damage. “However, an alternate trekking route starting from Kathmandu through Sundarijal, Helambu, Thadepati, Ghopte, Gosaikunda, Thulosyabru, Lama Hotel and onward to Langtang and Kyanjin is operational,” it said.

TAAN also said the Ganesh Himal and Ruby Valley areas are safe, but advised trekkers to bypass the closed Dhunche-Syabrubesi road by taking alternative routes via Dhadingbesi or Arughat in Gorkha.

The Manaslu and Tsum Valley regions are safe following repairs to the Chaurikharka landslide and the construction of two wooden bridges by local residents between Ghap and Namrung. “For safety reasons, trekkers are advised not to ride horses and to avoid using mules for transport on this section of the trail,” it said.

Stating that the standard road access to the trailhead has been affected, TAAN has advised trekkers to use alternative access routes such as Galchhi–Sunaulabazaar–Dhadingbesi–Salyantar–Arughat–Lapubesi or Benighat–Arughat–Lapubesi to reach the Manaslu trailhead.

TAAN said that all trekking trails in Manang and Mustang are safe and fully operational. “Although a recent earthquake in Upper Mustang damaged some private homes and monasteries, tourist infrastructure, lodges, trails and communication networks are fully operational,” it said.

The association has advised trekkers to fly directly to Pokhara or use the Benighat or Galchhi bypass routes, or travel south through Hetauda and Chitwan National Park, to reach Pokhara due to the collapse of the Prithvi Highway at Krishnabhir in Dhading.

TAAN also said the Rasuwagadhi-Kerung route for the Kailash-Mansarovar trip has been completely closed following the Bhotekoshi flood. “The Kodari-Tatopani route is open only for returning pilgrims entering Nepal,” it said. “Those heading to Kailash-Mansarovar can use the Simkot-Hilsa route via helicopter or road through Yalbang, or choose to fly into Lhasa and drive to Kailash through Shigatse and Saga.”

item.dc:creator: bishnu

The Sensitive Index, which measures the performance of blue-chip companies, also closed 1.1% higher. The benchmark index rose steadily in the final hour of trading after remaining largely […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: The Nepal Stock Exchange (Nepse) index snapped a two-day losing run on Friday, the last trading day of the week, closing 27.94 points higher at 2,559.49.

The Sensitive Index, which measures the performance of blue-chip companies, also closed 1.1% higher.

The benchmark index rose steadily in the final hour of trading after remaining largely range-bound during the middle of the session. Market breadth was positive, as 238 scrips advanced on Friday. Only 30 declined, while nine remained unchanged.

Trading activity also remained strong, as total turnover improved to Rs 4.36 billion, with 12.09 million units traded through 49,006 transactions.

Among individual stocks, Upakar Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha Ltd logged the biggest gain of 10.53%. Next were Aviyan Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha and Sindhu Bikash Bank, with gains of 10.09% and 9.54%, respectively. On the other hand, Multipurpose Finance Company Ltd posted the biggest loss of 5.71%. Emerging Nepal Ltd and Om Mega Pharmaceuticals followed with losses of 4.21% and 4%, respectively.

Liberty Energy Company topped the turnover chart with total transactions worth Rs 366.65 million. NRN Infrastructure & Development and Reliance Spinning Mills Ltd were next, with turnovers of Rs 185.1 million and Rs 147.95 million, respectively.

The sub-indices of all 13 trading groups ended the session in the green. The biggest gain came from the Hydropower Index, which closed 1.83% higher. The Non-life Insurance and Investment sub-indices were next, with gains of 1.72% and 1.58%, respectively.

The Sensitive Index, which measures the performance of blue-chip companies, also went down by 0.54%. The benchmark index opened higher but remained under pressure for most of the […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: The Nepal Stock Exchange (Nepse) index extended its losses for a second consecutive session on Thursday, falling 13.85 points, or 0.54%, to close at 2,531.55 points.

The Sensitive Index, which measures the performance of blue-chip companies, also went down by 0.54%.

The benchmark index opened higher but remained under pressure for most of the session. It reached an intraday high of around 2,546.1 points before falling to a low of around 2,525.21 points. Some late buying, however, helped erase some losses.

The decline came amid broad-based selling, with 200 stocks declining and 67 closing higher. Eleven stocks remained unchanged during the session. Total turnover slightly fell to Rs 4 billion. A total of 10.58 million units were traded through 44,198 transactions on Thursday.

Among individual stocks, Liberty Energy Company posted the biggest gain of the session, hitting a 15% positive circuit. Dolti Power Company Ltd and Upper Lohorekhola Hydropower Company followed with gains of 8.22% and 7.02%, respectively. On the other hand, Sindhu Bikash Bank posted the biggest loss, falling 14.98%. Prabhu Select Fund and Prabhu Smart Fund followed with losses of 10.22% and 9.3%, respectively.

Likewise, Liberty Energy Company topped the turnover chart with Rs 454.88 million. Reliance Spinning Mills Ltd and NRN Infrastructure & Development Ltd followed with turnovers of Rs 211.26 million and Rs 191.15 million, respectively.

All trading groups ended the session in the red. The biggest loss came from the Manufacturing & Processing sub-index, which closed 1.14% lower. Non-life Insurance and Finance sub-indices followed with losses of 0.78% and 0.66%, respectively.

item.title: Make RDNA of Bhotekoshi floods realistic, evidence-based: Wagle
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: Minister for Finance Swarnim Wagle has directed officials to make sure that the Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment (RDNA) of the physical damage caused by the Rasuwa floods is realistic and evidence-based. Wagle gave the direction during a discussion at the Finance Ministry on Tuesday on separate preliminary assessments being prepared by a task […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Minister for Finance Swarnim Wagle has directed officials to make sure that the Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment (RDNA) of the physical damage caused by the Rasuwa floods is realistic and evidence-based.

Wagle gave the direction during a discussion at the Finance Ministry on Tuesday on separate preliminary assessments being prepared by a task force formed by the National Planning Commission and the World Bank.

The task force is preparing an RDNA, while the World Bank has prepared a preliminary assessment under its Global Rapid Post-Disaster Damage Estimation (GRADE) methodology.

“An accurate assessment of the physical damage and needs caused by the floods is essential to make reconstruction and rehabilitation effective,” Wagle said, speaking at a discussion on preliminary assessments being prepared by a task force formed by the National Planning Commission and the World Bank on Wednesday. “The RDNA and GRADE assessments must be realistic and evidence-based and serve as a single national document so that the government can make sound decisions and mobilise investment.”

The National Planning Commission (NPC) is preparing a preliminary assessment framework covering the physical and human losses caused by the floods. The World Bank has already prepared its preliminary damage assessment.

The discussion was held to verify the initial findings of the two assessments and prepare a shared preliminary report.

According to NPC, RDNA is being conducted across four sectors: social, productive, infrastructure and cross-cutting.

The social sector covers damage to private buildings and structures, as well as public, education, health and cultural heritage infrastructure. Similarly, the productive sector assessment covers agriculture, fisheries, livestock, financial services and economic activities, while the infrastructure assessment covers hydropower projects and transmission lines, household renewable energy use, roads, bridges, telecommunications, environmental health, irrigation and river management. The assessment also covers cross-cutting issues like debris and hazardous waste accumulated in flood-affected areas.

The government plans to use the RDNA report to arrange immediate relief, mobilise investment resources and advance reconstruction and rehabilitation, according to the finance ministry.

item.title: LPG shortage due to non-cooperation by bottlers: Industry minister
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: Minister for Industry, Commerce and Supplies Gauri Kumari has attributed the current shortage of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) in Kathmandu Valley to non-cooperation by LPG bottlers. Speaking at a meeting of the Industry, Commerce, Labour and Consumer Welfare Committee of the House of Representatives on Wednesday, Minister Kumari said the government was unable to resolve […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Minister for Industry, Commerce and Supplies Gauri Kumari has attributed the current shortage of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) in Kathmandu Valley to non-cooperation by LPG bottlers.

Speaking at a meeting of the Industry, Commerce, Labour and Consumer Welfare Committee of the House of Representatives on Wednesday, Minister Kumari said the government was unable to resolve the shortage because all 58 gas bottlers are from the private sector. “There won’t have been any shortage had each of the 58 industries sent 3,000 cylinders to Kathmandu Valley every day as requested by the government,” she said. “But the bottlers refused our request.”

Minister Kumari claimed that of the 45,000 cylinders reportedly dispatched for Kathmandu on Monday and another 48,000 on Tuesday, only 19,000–20,000 had reached the market. “The government has not been able to determine where the remaining cylinders went,” she added.

She also said the industrialists had refused to provide details of LPG distribution. “The government has been left helpless,” she added.

Minister Kumari said the government must establish its own LPG bottling unit under Nepal Oil Corporation (NOC) to break the monopoly of private bottlers. “The country does not need more than two bottling industries. The remaining ones should be scrapped,” she said.

LPG, which was already in short supply due to global supply disruptions stemming from problems in the Strait of Hormuz, has become even scarcer in the market following the collapse of the Prithvi Highway at Krishnabhir in Dhading. The closure of the key artery linking Kathmandu to the rest of the country has disrupted the supply of LPG cylinders to the Valley, as large trucks carrying LPG are struggling to negotiate the narrow bends along the single-lane alternative routes designated by the government, say bottlers.

Commenting on sugar availability in the market, Minister Kumari said the cabinet has approved imports of 25,000 tons at 1% customs duty. “Supply arrangements are being made to make sure that the entire consignment is imported by the first week of October,” she added.
